mainTopic: End of the משנה on starting work before שבת, the ink-soaking (לש) question, and the debate over why a water mill may not run on שבת, including שביתת כלים
overview: This amud opens with the last lines of the משנה. בית הלל allow starting these processes on Friday 'while the sun is still shining.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that his family was stricter: they gave white clothes to a non-Jewish launderer three days before שבת. Both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that one may load the olive press and wine press before שבת. The גמרא first asks which תנא holds that just adding water to ink counts as kneading (לש). רב יוסף says it is רבי, but אביי suggests it could fit רבי יוסי too, and the proof from ashes is pushed aside. Next, a ברייתא lists processes that may keep going on שבת, except a water mill. רבה says the mill is forbidden because of its noise, and רב יוסף says it is because of שביתת כלים. The גמרא then explains that only a utensil that actively works is a problem. Finally, רב אושעיא teaches that only בית שמאי hold שביתת כלים, which sets up a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of בית הלל's ruling ('while the sun is still shining') and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's family custom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its previous ruling with the word 'the sun.' Then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reports that his father's household gave white clothes to a non-Jewish launderer at least three days before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...while there is still] the sun. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: My father's household had a custom to give white clothes to a non-Jewish launderer three days before שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes בית הלל's earlier ruling: all the listed cases (soaking ink, drying flax, dyeing wool, setting traps, giving clothes to a non-Jewish launderer) may be started on Friday as long as it is still daytime. Then it records the stricter personal custom of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's family about laundry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule of בית הלל is that a job started before שבת may continue by itself on שבת. Still, the house of the נשיא was extra careful with white clothes. White clothes take longer to clean, so the work would be more likely to run into שבת, and people might think the launderer was working for a Jew on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: While the sun is still shining, meaning while it is still daytime on Friday
My father's household (here, the family of the נְשִׂיאִים)

steps.confusionAlert: The first word, הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, is not a new statement. It is the last word of the previous line in the משנה ('as long as it is done while the sun is still shining').

phrases.english: [while there is still] the sun.
phrases.notes: This is the last word of בית הלל's ruling in the משנה ('ובית הלל מתירין עם השמש'), and it applies to all the cases listed.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
My father's household was accustomed
to give white clothes
to a non-Jewish launderer
three days before Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: נוֹהֲגִין הָיוּ בֵּית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf and adds a stricter family custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The house of רבן גמליאל gave white clothes to a non-Jewish launderer no later than three days before שבת.

steps.title: Both schools agree about loading the olive press and wine press
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי and בית הלל both allow loading the beam of the olive press and the wine press on ערב שבת, even though the squeezing continues on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both these and those (בית שמאי and בית הלל) agree that one may load the beam of the olive press and the round weights of the wine press.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a case where even the strict בית שמאי agree: one may set the press weights on Friday and let them keep pressing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually בית שמאי forbid starting work that will finish by itself on שבת. Here they agree to allow it. The olives were already crushed and the grapes already trodden before the weights were loaded, so the liquid would flow out even without them. Squeezing them further is therefore not the real מלאכה, even if it continues on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Both groups agree (בֵּית שַׁמַּאי and בֵּית הִלֵּל)
The heavy beam of the olive press
The round weights used in the wine press

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a case of agreement: even בית שמאי allow loading the presses before שבת.

phrases.english: And these and those agree,
that one may load the beam of the olive press
and the circular weights of the wine press.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁוִין אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a point both schools agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל allow loading the olive press and the wine press on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Who holds that adding water to ink counts as soaking it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that simply putting water into ink is already 'soaking,' a form of the מלאכה of לש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who holds that adding water to ink is the same as soaking it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking whose opinion stands behind the משנה's assumption that just pouring water into ink counts as soaking it. This question sets up the search that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה spoke about soaking ink, and it treated merely putting the water in as the forbidden act. That means the מלאכה of לש (kneading) is done just by adding the water, with no stirring needed. The גמרא wants to find which תנא holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תַּנָּא (whose opinion is this)?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Who is the tanna [who holds]
that putting water into ink
is itself their soaking?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא נְתִינַת מַיִם לִדְיוֹ זוֹ הִיא שְׁרִיָּיתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that adding water alone, with no kneading, counts as soaking (לש)?

steps.title: רב יוסף says it is רבי, proven from the flour-and-water case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the תנא is רבי. In a ברייתא, רבי makes the one who adds water to flour liable even without kneading, while רבי יוסי requires actual kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי. As a ברייתא teaches: If one person puts in the flour and another puts in the water, the second one is liable. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי says: He is not liable until he kneads.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question: the משנה follows רבי. He proves it from a ברייתא where רבי says adding water alone is enough to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the flour case, רבי holds that pouring in the water already counts as kneading, so the one who adds the water is liable. That matches the משנה's view on ink. רבי יוסי disagrees and requires real kneading, so he cannot be the author of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The last one (the one who adds the second ingredient) is liable

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key dispute of the sugya: does mixing a solid with water count as the מלאכה of לש by itself, or is real kneading needed?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi.
As it was taught [in a baraita]:
One person puts in the flour
and another puts in the water —
the latter is liable; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yosei says:
He is not liable until he kneads.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי, who holds that adding water alone makes one liable for לש.

steps.title: אביי: maybe רבי יוסי agrees in the case of ink
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that רבי יוסי may require real kneading only for flour, which can be kneaded. With ink, which cannot be kneaded, even רבי יוסי might hold that adding water is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But perhaps רבי יוסי only said this about flour, which can be kneaded. But ink, which cannot be kneaded, say that he would be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof. Maybe the משנה could follow רבי יוסי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed רבי יוסי always requires real kneading. אביי points out a difference: flour can actually be kneaded, so for flour the real kneading is the key act. Ink cannot be kneaded, so pouring in the water may be the whole act. If so, even רבי יוסי would make one liable for ink, and the משנה would not have to follow רבי alone.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling up to this point (only in this case)
Say that he should be liable

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: But perhaps Rabbi Yosei only stated [his view]
regarding flour, which can be kneaded.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דְּיוֹ דְּלָאו בַּר גִּיבּוּל הוּא,
phrases.english: But ink, which cannot be kneaded,
say he would be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְדִילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's proof that the משנה follows only רבי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must follow רבי and cannot follow רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The flour case may not apply to ink, because ink cannot be kneaded.

steps.title: Proof from the ashes case: real kneading is required even for something that cannot be kneaded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's suggestion using a ברייתא about ashes and water, where רבי יהודה's son רבי יוסי still requires real kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think this. As a ברייתא teaches: If one person puts in the ashes and another puts in the water, the second one is liable. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי the son of רבי יהודה says: [He is not liable] until he kneads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי. Even with ashes, which cannot be kneaded, the dissenting view still requires actual kneading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes are like ink: they cannot really be kneaded. Even so, the dissenting תנא says one is liable only after real kneading. That shows אביי's distinction does not work, and the משנה about ink must follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not let this enter your mind (this is not correct)

steps.confusionAlert: The dissenter here is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, not the רבי יוסי of the flour ברייתא. The גמרא still treats his view as the same approach to kneading.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
as it was taught [in a baraita]:
One person puts in the ashes
and another puts in the water —
the latter is liable; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
[He is not liable] until he kneads.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב יוסף against אביי's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The dissenting view requires real kneading even for things that cannot be kneaded, so the ink משנה follows רבי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about ashes and water.

steps.title: Maybe 'ashes' really means soil, which can be kneaded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אפר (ashes) in the ברייתא might really mean עפר (soil), which can be kneaded. If so, the proof falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps what does 'ashes' mean? Soil, which can be kneaded?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ashes proof. Maybe the ברייתא's word means soil, which would put it back in the 'can be kneaded' category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words אפר and עפר look and sound very similar. If the ברייתא is really about soil, it is like flour, and אביי's distinction stands again.

phrases.english: But perhaps, what is 'ashes' —
soil, which can be kneaded?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא מַאי ״אֵפֶר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be speaking about soil, which can be kneaded.

steps.title: Both versions exist: one says ashes, another says soil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one ברייתא says אפר and another says עפר, so the dispute applies to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one ברייתא teaches 'ashes,' and another ברייתא teaches 'soil'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ashes proof. There are two separate versions, so 'ashes' should not be read as 'soil.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one ברייתא says 'ashes' and a different one says 'soil,' then both are meant literally. The dispute would then cover real ashes too, and the proof against אביי returns.

phrases.english: But was it not taught 'ashes,'
and was it not taught 'soil'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא ״אֵפֶר״, וְהָתַנְיָא ״עָפָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ashes proof against step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The word 'ashes' in the ברייתא means real ashes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that there are two ברייתות, one saying אפר and one saying עפר.

steps.title: The two versions were not taught side by side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the defense: the two ברייתות were not taught next to each other, so they may just be two wordings of the same case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were they taught next to each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא weakens the defense again. The two versions come from different places, so they might be the same ברייתא with a variant spelling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both cases appeared together in one list, they would clearly be two separate rulings. Since they come from separate sources, 'ashes' may simply be another version of 'soil.' The proof against אביי falls away, and the גמרא drops the topic here. The next step starts a new ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Were they taught next to each other?

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף says the ink משנה follows רבי. אביי argues it could also fit רבי יוסי. The ashes proof against אביי is rejected, so אביי's possibility stays standing and the גמרא moves on.

phrases.english: Were they taught next to each other?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense given in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that two ברייתות prove the dispute covers real ashes.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two ברייתות are from separate sources and may be wording variants of one teaching.

steps.title: Processes started before שבת may continue on שבת, except a water mill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists cases where you may start something on ערב שבת that keeps working all of שבת: water flowing into a garden, מוגמר perfuming clothes, גפרית coloring vessels, קילור on the eye and a bandage on a wound. A water mill is different: you may only put in wheat if it will be ground before שבת begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: You may open a water channel into a garden on Friday at dusk, and it keeps filling all day. You may put incense under clothes on Friday, and they keep getting perfumed all day. You may put sulfur under vessels on Friday at dusk, and they keep getting sulfured all of שבת. You may put eye salve on an eye and a bandage on a wound on Friday at dusk, and it keeps healing all day. But you may not put wheat into a water mill unless it will be ground while it is still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes a ברייתא. It lists things you may start before שבת that keep going on שבת, plus one exception: the water mill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that a process started before שבת may continue on its own during שבת. The water mill is the one case that breaks the rule. The next steps try to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: incense or spices burned on coals to perfume clothes
sulfur, used to whiten or color silver vessels
a mill turned by water power

steps.confusionAlert: None of the allowed cases involves doing work on שבת. Everything is set up before שבת. The question is only whether the process may keep going by itself.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One may open water into a garden
on Shabbat eve at nightfall
and it keeps filling up all day long

phrases.aramaic: וּמַנִּיחִין מוּגְמָר תַּחַת הַכֵּלִים עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: and one may place incense under the clothes on Shabbat eve
and they keep getting perfumed all day long
and one may place sulfur under the vessels
on Shabbat eve at nightfall
and they keep getting sulfured all of Shabbat
and one may place eye salve on the eye
and a bandage on a wound
on Shabbat eve at nightfall
and it keeps healing all day long
But one may not put wheat
into a water mill
unless it is enough that they will be ground while it is still day

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פּוֹתְקִין מַיִם לַגִּינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic after the ink and kneading discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Processes set up before שבת may continue by themselves on שבת, except grinding in a water mill.

steps.title: Why is the water mill different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the water mill is forbidden when all the other ongoing processes are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: what makes the mill different from the other cases?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case the work happens by itself on שבת. So the mill must have some special feature, and the גמרא wants to find it.

keyTerms.meaning: while it is still day (before שבת)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why is the mill forbidden when the others are allowed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the exception in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the water mill is forbidden while the other processes are allowed.

steps.title: רבה: the mill makes noise
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the mill is forbidden because it makes noise. People hear grinding on שבת, and that is disrespectful to the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Because it makes a noise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his reason: a mill is loud, so everyone can hear work happening on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garden, perfume, sulfur and bandage all work quietly. A mill announces itself, which looks like a public disgrace of שבת. So the חכמים forbade it, even though no person is actually doing work.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes a noise (it is heard)

phrases.english: Rabbah said: Because it makes a noise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּשְׁמַעַת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mill is forbidden because of its noise, a rabbinic concern about public disgrace of שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: why not say it is because utensils must rest?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבה. Why not use a stronger reason, שביתת כלים? A ברייתא learns from the פסוק 'ובכל אשר אמרתי אליכם תשמרו' that a Jew's utensils must also rest on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Let the master say it is because of the resting of utensils! As it was taught: 'And in all that I have said to you, take heed' comes to include the resting of utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on רבה. He offers a different and stronger reason: the mill is a Jew's utensil, and it must not work on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reason (noise) is only a rabbinic concern about how things look. רב יוסף points to a source in a פסוק showing that a Jew's utensils may not do forbidden work on שבת. The mill is the utensil doing the grinding, so that should be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the rule that a Jew's utensils must 'rest' (not do forbidden work) on שבת
let the master say (why not say?)
to include (an extra case learned from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
Let the master say: because of the resting of utensils!
As it was taught: 'And in all that I have said to you, take heed'
this comes to include the resting of utensils.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: וְלֵימָא מָר מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִיתַת כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer by offering a better reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that the mill is forbidden because of noise.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a stronger, Torah-based reason available (שביתת כלים), so why fall back on noise?

steps.title: רב יוסף's own reason: utensils must rest
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף states his own view: the mill is forbidden because of שביתת כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Because of the resting of utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records רב יוסף's own answer to 'what is the reason?': the mill is forbidden because the utensil must rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two explanations for the mill: רבה says noise, רב יוסף says שביתת כלים. רב יוסף's view raises a new problem, and the next step takes it up.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Because of the resting of utensils.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִיתַת כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Records רב יוסף's own answer, replacing רבה's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The water mill is forbidden because of שביתת כלים.

steps.title: Then why are sulfur and incense allowed?
steps.stepSummary: If בית הלל hold that שביתת כלים is דאורייתא, why may sulfur and incense keep working under the vessels and clothes on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you say בית הלל hold that resting of utensils is a Torah law, why did they permit sulfur and incense?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב יוסף's approach. If utensils must rest, the sulfur and incense cases in the ברייתא look like a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (which follows בית הלל) allows sulfur and incense to burn all שבת, and they sit in utensils. If utensils must rest by Torah law, how can that be allowed?

phrases.english: Now that you have said
that Beit Hillel hold
resting of utensils as Torah law,
why did they permit sulfur and incense?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְבֵית הִלֵּל אִית לְהוּ שְׁבִיתַת כֵּלִים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב יוסף's reason against the permitted cases of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית הלל hold שביתת כלים is דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sulfur and incense keep working in utensils on שבת, yet the ברייתא allows them.

steps.title: The utensil is not doing any action
steps.stepSummary: Sulfur and incense are allowed because the utensil itself does no action. It just holds the coals while they burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it does not perform an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: שביתת כלים only forbids a utensil that actively does the work, and here the utensil does nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows שביתת כלים. The rule is not broken just because work happens near or inside a utensil. It applies only when the utensil itself performs the action, like a mill turning and grinding.
steps.whatToRemember: Under שביתת כלים, only a utensil that actively performs the work is a problem. A utensil that just sits there is fine.

phrases.english: Because it does not perform an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא קָעָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any forbidden work happening in a utensil breaks שביתת כלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a utensil that actively performs the action breaks שביתת כלים.

steps.title: Why are bundles of flax in the oven allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it is allowed to put bundles of flax in an oven before שבת to dry on שבת, even though the oven is a utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bundles of flax: what is the reason they permitted them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another permitted case, flax drying in an oven, and asks how it fits with שביתת כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flax keeps drying inside a utensil (the oven) all שבת. The גמרא checks whether the new principle covers this case too.

phrases.aramaic: אוּנִּין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן מַאי טַעְמָא שָׁרוּ
phrases.english: Bundles of flax: what is the reason they permitted?
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה about putting flax in an oven before שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוּנִּין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן מַאי טַעְמָא שָׁרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question to another permitted case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How flax drying in an oven fits with שביתת כלים.

steps.title: The oven just sits still
steps.stepSummary: The flax is allowed for the same reason: the oven does no action. It just rests in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it does not perform an action, and it sits at rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the oven is passive. It sits still while the flax dries by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oven does not move or work. The heat inside it does the drying on its own. So the same principle covers this case.

phrases.english: Because it does not perform an action,
and it simply sits at rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה, וּמֵינָח נַיְיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with the same principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oven is passive, so שביתת כלים is not broken.

steps.title: But traps do perform an action
steps.stepSummary: Traps for animals, birds and fish actively catch. So why may they be set before שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: Traps for animals, birds and fish, which do perform an action: what is the reason they permitted them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new principle with a harder case: a trap really does act when it snaps shut and catches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה allows setting traps before שבת. A trap does seem to perform an action, so the principle seems to fail here.

phrases.english: Traps for an animal, a bird and fish
which do perform an action,
what is the reason they permitted them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצוּדַת חַיָּה וְעוֹף וְדָגִים דְּקָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'no action' principle with a case where the utensil seems to act.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that only an active utensil breaks שביתת כלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Traps actively catch, yet they are allowed, so the principle seems not to fit.

steps.title: The permitted traps are hooks and nets that do not move
steps.stepSummary: The permitted traps are a fishhook and nets, which stay still. The animal comes to them by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it refers to a hook and nets, which do not perform an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means traps that just sit in place, not ones that snap shut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hook or a net does not move. The fish swims into it and is caught. A trap that actually moves to catch would indeed be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: nets or traps that stay in place

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying traps are never a problem. It limits the permission to passive traps. An active trap would be forbidden.

phrases.english: There too, it refers to a hook and nets
which do not perform an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי בְּלֶחִי וְקוּקְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The permitted traps are active traps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitted traps are passive hooks and nets.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the system under the assumption that בית הלל hold שביתת כלים is דאורייתא: active utensils are forbidden, passive ones are allowed.

steps.title: רב אושעיא: only בית שמאי hold utensils must rest
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא in the name of רב אסי says that the תנא who holds שביתת כלים is דאורייתא is בית שמאי, not בית הלל. So for בית שמאי any utensil working on שבת is forbidden, active or not. For בית הלל it is allowed, even if the utensil is active.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that רב אושעיא said that רב אסי said: Who is the תנא who holds resting of utensils is Torah law? It is בית שמאי and not בית הלל. So according to בית שמאי, whether it performs an action or not, it is forbidden. According to בית הלל, even if it performs an action, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new view that changes the picture. Only בית שמאי hold that utensils must rest, and בית הלל do not hold this at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we assumed בית הלל hold שביתת כלים and only active utensils are a problem. Now we learn that בית הלל do not hold it at all, so even active utensils are fine for them. בית שמאי are strict in every case, active or passive.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא (whose view is this)?

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אושעיא: בית שמאי forbid every working utensil on שבת, and בית הלל allow even an active one.

phrases.english: And now that
Rav Oshaya said that Rav Asi said:
Who is the Tanna who holds resting of utensils is Torah law?

phrases.aramaic: — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא וְלָא בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: It is Beit Shammai, and not Beit Hillel.
According to Beit Shammai, whether it performs an action
or it does not perform an action, it is forbidden.
According to Beit Hillel, even though
it performs an action, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the assumption of step 15 that בית הלל hold שביתת כלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שביתת כלים is דאורייתא only according to בית שמאי. בית שמאי forbid even passive utensils, and בית הלל permit even active ones.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge to בית שמאי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge. If בית שמאי forbid even a passive utensil, then something else seems to follow. The challenge itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that you said that according to בית שמאי, even though it does not perform an action it is forbidden, if so,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to challenge בית שמאי's strict view, and the actual question comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because בית שמאי forbid even passive utensils, the גמרא is about to point to a case where that would cause a problem. The words 'אי הכי' signal that a difficulty is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (signals a challenge is coming)

phrases.english: And now that you have said
that according to Beit Shammai, even though
it does not perform an action, it is forbidden,
if so,
phrases.notes: The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ דִּלְבֵית שַׁמַּאי אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה אָסוּר אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב אושעיא's statement to set up a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's view that even passive utensils must rest.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a passive utensil is forbidden, some practice will contradict it. The specific case comes on the next amud.
